name: VerseOrder
subtitle: The Ultimate Marvel Multiverse Watch Order
editorialNotice: 112-entry narrative watch order updated through October 17, 2026. New additions are source-checked; the older 110-entry baseline still awaits a comprehensive editorial audit.

entries.title: Marvel One-Shot: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to Thor's Hammer
Marvel One-Shot: All Hail the King
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
The Amazing Spider-Man 2 (2014)
entries.note: It ends on an unresolved cliffhanger because Sony canceled the reboot before a third film. Andrew Garfield's catharsis comes in No Way Home. Do not expect closure here.
entries.whyHere: This story does not resolve every arc on its own; the later multiverse films provide additional context.

entries.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
entries.whyHere: The earlier Spider-Man and Venom stories are placed just before this entry so the multiverse payoff carries more weight.

entries.title: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
entries.whyHere: An optional companion that offers a fresh perspective on parallel realities before the next multiverse stories.

entries.title: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
Fantastic Four (2005, Chris Evans as Johnny Storm)
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007)
X-Men: Days of Future Past
entries.whyHere: Watching the original story first makes the consequences of this turning point more meaningful.

entries.title: Logan
entries.whyHere: Placed immediately before Deadpool & Wolverine to preserve the emotional weight of the characters' journey.

entries.title: The Fantastic Four: First Steps
entries.note: Set on Earth-828, a retro-futuristic alternate universe inspired by the 1960s.

entries.title: VisionQuest S1
entries.note: Streaming weekly; only the first 2 of 8 episodes had premiered as of 2026-10-17.
entries.whyHere: A continuation of the WandaVision and Agatha All Along storyline. Placed in the late-MCU section to preserve the character arc without separating it from the next chapter.

entries.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
entries.note: Released July 31, 2026; follows the story of No Way Home.
entries.whyHere: Continues Peter Parker's story after No Way Home. Its urban-MCU connections benefit from watching the later Daredevil and Punisher stories first.
